title: Kernel Pinning Advisor: layer-to-kernel affinity and staged rollout for FlashAttention v2/v3
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We continue to see sporadic latency regressions and prefill stalls on certain model-layer / input-shape combinations after enabling FlashAttention v3. Root causes range from suboptimal kernel choice for long-head counts, workspace fragmentation, to decoder prefill/decode scheduling interactions. Purpose: build a conservative 'Kernel Pinning Advisor' that recommends and can enact per-layer kernel affinities (v2 vs v3 vs fallback) backed by deterministic perf runs and telemetry thresholds, and provide a safe staged rollout mechanism with automatic rollback triggers.
background: Previous work focused on runtime kernel prober, warmup smoothing, and gated scheduler heuristics. Those mitigations reduced noise but left cases where the heuristic selector oscillates across requests leading to jittery latency tail. Pinning at layer granularity can lock in a validated kernel for sensitive layers during canaries while preserving global selector for non-sensitive layers.
acceptance_criteria: Advisor produces an immutable layer->kernel affinity map for a given model/version and stores it in the runtime config
End-to-end canary flow to apply affinity map to 1% of traffic and collect latency/p99/token-cost/ooms/stalls metrics
Automatic rollback if p99 increases by >10% or stall-rate >0.1% vs baseline over 30 minutes
Integration tests validating functional parity for small, medium, large heads/seq-lens for both v2 and v3 pinned layers
Playbook documenting how to review advisor recommendations and how to run local perf harness on a dev machine
tasks: Design advisor heuristics: cost/latency tradeoff function that ingests microbenchmarks and live telemetry
Implement layer fingerprinting: canonical name, head-count, hidden-size, layer-index and preferred input shapes
Create deterministic perf harness that sweeps head/seq/workspace settings for v2/v3 and records stable metrics
Store affinity maps in config-store and expose API for canary application (runtime flag per-deployment)
Build canary orchestration: traffic split, metrics collection, rollback triggers and notification hooks
Add telemetry dashboards: pinned vs auto-selected comparison (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, stall-rate, OOMs)
E2E tests: CI job that runs small model with pinned map and validates output equality and no regressions beyond tolerance
Docs + runbook: reviewer checklist, safe thresholds, escalation path and postmortem template
notes: Heuristic idea: prefer v3 for layers where v3_latency < v2_latency * 0.95 AND v3_memory_overhead < 1.15x, otherwise prefer stable v2. Tag ambiguous layers as 'adaptive' (runtime selector allowed).

Must consider mixed decoding: when prefill uses kernel A and decode chooses kernel B, check KV cache layout and migration cost. If migration cost > jitter budget then advisor should pin both phases to same kernel for that layer.
Canary safety: start with synthetic traffic that mirrors production shape distribution for target customer before opening 1% live traffic
Telemetry sources: prefills_per_min, decode_tokens_per_min, kernel_switch_count, stall_events, p99_latency_by_layer, workspace_alloc_failures
Related incident: prod-2026-02-21-prefill-spike — attached in related_links
Trade-offs: pinning reduces adaptability and may miss future good gains from v3 improvements. To mitigate, advisor will produce TTLs for affinity maps and schedule periodic re-eval windows.
Risk: affinity map misapplied across model variants; include model_hash validation before applying map.
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Ticket created. Scoping meeting with Serving Runtime and Observability teams. Decided advisor will live in runtime config service and be surfaced in Console as 'Pinned Kernel Overrides'.
2026-03-11: Prototype perf harness completed (single-GPU synthetic sweep). Initial data shows v3 is ~12% faster for short sequences but regresses for head_count>64 on some layouts.
2026-03-12: Mateo pushed draft PR for layer fingerprinting schema: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/4237. Asking infra for config-store quota for affinity maps.

2026-03-13: Discussed rollback thresholds with SRE. Agreed: automatic rollback if p99 > baseline * 1.10 or stall-rate delta > 0.001 (0.1%). Added ticket to add synthetic prefill scenarios to canary harness.
owner_notes: Longer-term: expose advisor suggestions in Console QA tab and permit customer-level overrides for Dedicated/Private deployments. Consider a ML model to predict best kernel given telemetry and microbenchmarks as a follow-up.
